chunks: 4 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who made a bequest to another man of a fixed bequest, unspecified in amount, from his wealth, whether one-third, one-quarter, less than that, or more. Then the testator was killed, and blood money (diyah) was paid for him. He ruled regarding his bequest: 'That it is executed from his wealth and his blood money, just as he bequeathed.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٌ مَقْطُوعَةٌ: Fixed bequest (a specific portion of the estate)

ai.seo_question: How is a bequest fulfilled if the testator is killed and receives blood money?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the concept of *diyah* (blood money) is treated as an extension of the deceased's estate (*mal*), ensuring that a bequest made without a fixed sum is fulfilled from both the original assets and the compensation received for his death. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that *diyah* inherits the legal status of the deceased's property, allowing bequests to attach to it just as they would to real estate or cash. The ruling underscores the continuity of financial obligations and rights even after death, reinforcing the integrity of the testator's intent.
